## Goal

In the herdr selection list, items with `status = in-progress` and `stage = in_review` must be included in the mandatory in_review set (always shown regardless of `browseItemCount`), just like `completed`/`in_review` items.

## Problem

Items being re-worked after review feedback keep `stage = in_review` but flip `status` to `in-progress` (per the project workflow, WL-0MSKCRX730052IIW). The smart-selection mandatory set only matches `status === 'completed' && stage === 'in_review'`:

- `smart-selection.ts`: `isMandatoryItem()` and the `reviews` filter in `selectWorkItems()` require `status === 'completed'`.
- `fetcher.ts`: `reviewQueueArgs()` / `fetchMandatorySubsets()` fetch `wl list --status completed --stage in_review --root-only`, so in-progress/in_review items aren't in the guaranteed subset at all.

As a result an in-progress/in_review item can be dropped from the default list when the `browseItemCount` window fills — it only survives as a capped "others" row. Only the stage-filtered `/wl in_review` view shows them reliably.

## Acceptance criteria

- AC1: `isMandatoryItem()` returns true for `status = in-progress` + `stage = in_review` (as well as `completed` + `in_review`, and critical).
- AC2: `selectWorkItems()` always includes in_progress/in_review items in the guaranteed review set (unbounded by `browseItemCount`), without double-counting items already in the critical set.
- AC3: `fetchMandatorySubsets()`/`reviewQueueArgs()` fetches `--status completed,in-progress` for the in_review mandatory subset so the fetch layer matches the selection-layer guarantee.
- AC4: The duplicative "another copy lives in the Pi TUI Worklog extension" note in `smart-selection.ts` is corrected — that copy was removed by WL-0MSGI7PV9004UD0N, so only the herdr copy (and the core `wl next` grouping duplication noted in `grouping.ts`) remains.
- AC5: All tests pass (update `smart-selection.test.ts`, fetcher tests, grouping regressions as needed; add coverage for in-progress/in_review included in the mandatory set).
data.title: Herdr selection list: include in_progress/in_review items in the mandatory In Review set

data.description:
## Goal

Actively-worked work items (status = in-progress) must be guaranteed a place in the herdr default selection list even when the mandatory review queue saturates `browseItemCount`.

## Problem

`fetchNextItems(count)` → `selectWorkItems(merged, count)` guarantees critical and in_review items are always shown (unbounded by `browseItemCount`), but every other item (including actively-worked `in-progress` items, which render in the "Group N" section) competes for the capped "others" budget:

```
othersLimit = max(0, browseItemCount - (criticals.length + reviews.length))
```

When the review queue is deep (root in_review count ≥ browseItemCount), `othersLimit` drops to 0 and ALL "others" are cut — an actively-worked item (e.g. `status=in-progress, stage=plan_complete`) vanishes from the default list even though `wl next --include-in-progress` returns it first. Observed with WL-0MV28X3SL005R5KX (22 mandatory reviews vs browseItemCount 20 → 0 others shown). Additionally, `wl next -n N` hard-caps at 32 items, so a low-priority in-progress item can fall outside the top-N base window altogether.

Actively-worked items are the producer's most important real-time signal ("what am I working on right now") — losing them from the list is worse than showing a slightly longer list.

## Acceptance criteria

- AC1: `selectWorkItems()` always includes items with `status = in-progress` (regardless of stage, not `done`) in the returned list — unbounded by `browseItemCount`, deduplicated against critical/in_review items (counts once when an item matches multiple criteria).
- AC2: `isMandatoryItem()` returns true for `status = in-progress` items (plus the existing critical and in_progress/in_review cases).
- AC3: Ordering within the mandatory additions: criticals first, then in_review reviews, then actively-worked in-progress items, then capped others — so the Group N (actively-worked) section still renders ahead of "Other" after regrouping.
- AC4: `fetchMandatorySubsets()` also fetches actively-worked root items explicitly (`wl list --status in-progress --root-only`), so an in-progress item is surfaced by `fetchNextItems()` even when it falls outside the `wl next` top-N window and even when review-queue depth pushes `othersLimit` to 0. `fetchReviewQueueState` is unaffected (its query stays shared with the mandatory review subset — the in-progress fetch is a separate, additional query).
- AC5: All tests pass, including new coverage for the review-queue-saturation scenario, the in-progress item outside the `wl next` window, and the overlap cases.
data.title: Herdr selection list: always show actively-worked in-progress items even when review queue saturates the window

The Herdr worklist selection list calls wl next to populate its results. wl next excludes dependency-blocked items by default (filterCandidates removes them unless includeBlocked is true). This means the Herdr selection list never shows dependency-blocked items, even though the user may need to see what is blocking their backlog.

Acceptance Criteria:

2. Blocked items are rendered with a visible indicator (status icon) so their state is clear.
3. The change is confined to the fetchNextItems invocation in fetcher.ts - no other callers of wl next are affected.
4. Unit tests cover the new --include-blocked flag in the args array.

Notes:
The change adds --include-blocked to the wl next args in fetchNextItems() (packages/herdr/src/fetcher.ts). status=blocked items were already included by wl next (the pipeline only penalises them with -10000); the gap is dependency-blocked items that are excluded entirely. Blocked items will rank low (penalised) by default scoring, so they appear at the bottom of the list.

data.description:
Inconsistency between the Herdr in_review stage filter and the ship release gate:

- The ship skill queries "wl list --stage in_review" with NO status filter (check-audit-gate.js, check-final-validation.js, generate-changelog.js), so a status=blocked item in the in_review stage (e.g. WL-0MTF5WO1N0088P5P) IS seen by the release gate and blocks the release.
- The Herdr in_review stage filter (fetchItemsByStage -> STAGE_STATUS.in_review = "completed,in-progress,open") EXCLUDES status=blocked items, so the same item never appears in the in_review filtered selection list.

The user-facing symptom: an in_review item that blocks the release is invisible in the /wl review view, so the selection list and the release gate disagree about what is in the review queue.

User story: As a Herdr user, I want the in_review filter to show every root item the ship release gate sees in in_review, so the selection list and the release gate agree on the review queue.

Acceptance Criteria:
1. fetchItemsByStage(in_review) issues a wl list query whose status filter includes blocked alongside completed/in-progress/open (verified by a unit test asserting the exec args).
2. A status=blocked root item at stage=in_review appears in the stage-filtered in_review list.
3. Other stages keep their existing status rules unchanged.
4. The stage-filter documentation (STAGE_STATUS comment in fetcher.ts, worklist.ts doc, packages/herdr/README.md) reflects that in_review includes blocked items.
5. Build passes and the herdr package test suite is green.

Notes:
- Root cause: STAGE_STATUS.in_review omits blocked. The project workflow (AGENTS.md, WL-0MSKCRX730052IIW) documented blocked as excluded, but the release gate does not exclude it — the exclusion makes release-blocking items invisible in the review filter.
- Fix: STAGE_STATUS.in_review = completed,in-progress,open,blocked. discovered-from:WL-0MV6TFX0600145M2
data.title: Herdr in_review filter hides blocked items that the release gate treats as release-blocking

data.description:
Follow-up to WL-0MV6TFX0600145M2. Adding --include-blocked to wl next made blocked items ELIGIBLE, but the default worklist still does not show a low-ranked blocked item such as WL-0MTF5WO1N0088P5P (status=blocked, stage=in_review, rank ~35 of 52):

- The base feed is `wl next -n <browseItemCount>` (default 20): the ranked #35 item is cut before it ever enters the pool.
- The mandatory subsets (critical, completed/in_review, in-progress) do not include status=blocked items, so smart selection cannot surface it either.
- Only the /wl review stage filter shows it (fixed in WL-0MV70XY6D008013C).

Per the operator: an in_review item blocks the release, so it must either appear in the list or not be in_review. It IS in_review, therefore it must appear in the DEFAULT list too.

User story: As a Herdr user, I want status=blocked root items always visible in the default worklist (like critical / in_review-completed / in-progress items), so release-blocking work can never be hidden by ranking or count caps.

Acceptance Criteria:
1. fetchMandatorySubsets() fetches status=blocked root-only items (wl list --status blocked --root-only) alongside the existing mandatory subsets.
2. selectWorkItems / isMandatoryItem treat status=blocked as mandatory: a blocked root item is always shown regardless of browseItemCount and rank.
3. The default worklist shows a low-ranked blocked in_review root item (regression test).
4. Non-blocked items keep existing behaviour (order, caps).
5. Build passes and the herdr package test suite is green.

Notes:
- discovered-from:WL-0MV6TFX0600145M2
- Also requires the user to close/reopen (or restart the herdr server to respawn) the worklist pane for new code to load: tsx runs without --watch, so an already-open pane keeps the old code.
